iast: caitanyaṃ svatantraṃ viśvottīrṇaṃ viśvagaṃ viśvabījam
english: Consciousness is autonomous, transcending the universe, pervading the universe, and the seed of the universe.

devanagari: इच्छा ज्ञानं क्रिया चैव त्रितयं शक्तिलक्षणम्
iast: icchā jñānaṃ kriyā caiva tritayaṃ śaktilakṣaṇam
english: Will, knowledge, and action — these three are the characteristics of Śakti.

devanagari: शाम्भवं शाक्तमाणवं च त्रिधोपायं वदन्ति हि
iast: śāmbhavaṃ śāktamāṇavaṃ ca tridhopāyaṃ vadanti hi
english: They speak of the means (upāya) as threefold: Śāmbhava (divine will), Śākta (empowered thought), and Āṇava (individual effort).

devanagari: अनुपायस्तु यः प्रोक्तः स शाम्भवपदं स्मृतम्
iast: anupāyastu yaḥ proktaḥ sa śāmbhavapadaṃ smṛtam
english: That which is called 'no means' (anupāya) is considered the state of Śāmbhava itself — the recognition that was never absent.

devanagari: परा वाग् वैखरी मध्या पश्यन्ती च चतुर्विधा
iast: parā vāg vaikharī madhyā paśyantī ca caturvidhā
english: Speech (vāc) is fourfold: Parā (transcendent), Paśyantī (visionary), Madhyamā (inner), and Vaikharī (gross).

iast: pratibhā saiva saṃvittiḥ prakāśate svatantrataḥ
english: Pratibhā (creative intuition) is consciousness itself, shining forth autonomously.

iast: kuṇḍalinī parā śaktiḥ svātmany eva vyavasthitā
english: Kuṇḍalinī is the supreme Energy (Śakti), established in the Self itself.

iast: trayastriṃśattattvāni śivāntāni prakīrtitāḥ
english: The Thirty-six Principles (tattvas) are declared, culminating in Śiva — from Earth to the Supreme.

devanagari: शिवः शक्तिः सदाशिव ईश्वरश्च शुद्धविद्या च पञ्चकम्
iast: śivaḥ śaktiḥ sadāśiva īśvaraś ca śuddhavidyā ca pañcakam
english: Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, and Śuddhavidyā — these five are the pure (śuddha) tattvas.

devanagari: माया कला विद्या रागः कालो नियतिरित्यमी कञ्चुकाः
iast: māyā kalā vidyā rāgaḥ kālo niyatir ity amī kañcukāḥ
english: Māyā, Kalā, Vidyā, Rāga, Kāla, and Niyati — these are the six coverings (kañcukas) that limit consciousness into finite experience.

iast: yaḥ syād vimarśarūpo 'sau svātmany eva prakāśate
english: That which is of the nature of self-awareness (vimarśa) shines forth in its own Self alone.

iast: dvādaśāntaṃ paraṃ sthānaṃ kuṇḍalyā vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: The wise know the End of the Twelve (dvādaśānta, twelve finger-widths above the head) as the supreme place of Kuṇḍalinī.

iast: samastajagadādhāraṃ sarvaśaktisamanvitam
english: It is the support of the entire universe, endowed with all powers (śaktis).

iast: viṣayeṣu vikalpānāṃ saṃskāraḥ śākta ucyate
english: The purification of thought-constructs (vikalpasaṃskāra) with respect to objects is called the Empowered Means (Śāktopāya).

iast: aṇupāyaḥ smṛto dehe mantradhyānādisādhanaiḥ
english: The Individual Means (Āṇavopāya) is taught as practice through the body, mantra, meditation, and other supports.

iast: na kiñcid api cinvānaḥ svātmany eva nilīyate
english: Contemplating nothing at all, one merges into one's own Self — this is the Divine Means (Śāmbhavopāya).

iast: prakāśavimarśamayī parā saṃvit prakāśate
english: The Supreme Consciousness, consisting of light (prakāśa) and self-awareness (vimarśa), shines forth.

devanagari: यथा यथा निवर्तते तथा तथा प्रकाशते
iast: yathā yathā nivartate tathā tathā prakāśate
english: In whatever way the mind turns away (from objects), in that very way consciousness shines forth.

iast: śivaḥ svatantraḥ kartā ca jñānakriyāsamanvitaḥ
english: Śiva is autonomous, the agent, endowed with knowledge (jñāna) and action (kriyā).

iast: saiva śaktiḥ parā proktā sarvajñānakriyātmikā
english: That very Śakti is called the Supreme, consisting of all knowledge and all action.
